MINUTES
  REGULAR PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  April 17, 2017

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
  called to order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR POPE.

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Retz, Persichina, Chair Pope, Giglia, Romanelli, and Wroan

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Portugal

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director

  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES, MARCH 20, 2017

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER GIGLIA

  TO APPROVE THE PARK & ACTIVITES MEETING MINUTES OF
  MARCH 20, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR POPE SO ORDERED.

  AUDIENCE ITEMS/WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  None.

  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  RECREATION FEES REVIEW

 Community Services Director Clark provided the Park & Activities Commission with a report
 discussing the increase in recreation fees. At an earlier Race Subcommittee meeting, there was
 further discussion on increasing the rate for pre-registration for the Hills Are Alive Race from $30
 to $35.

 Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission make a
 recommendation to City Council to increase the Youth Sports Organization sports fields usage
 fees and the sports field hourly rental fees by 2% and to consider increasing the pre-registration
 rate for the Hills Are Alive Race from $30 to $35.

 Commissioner Retz commented that the rate for the race is quite reasonable compared to the
 cost of other races.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER GIGLIA

 TO MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO INCREASE THE YOUTH
 SPORTS ORGANIZATION SPORTS FIELDS USAGE FEES AND THE SPORTS FIELD
 HOURLY RENTAL FEES BY 2% AND TO INCREASE THE PRE-REGISTRATION RATE FOR
 THE HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE FROM $30 TO $35.

  AYES:  RETZ, PERSICHINA, CHAIR POPE, GIGLIA, ROMANELLI
  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:
  ABSENT:  WROAN, PORTUGAL

  B.  MOVIE NIGHT FILM SELECTION

 Commissioner Wroan joined the meeting at 7:08 p.m.

 Director Clark asked the Planning Commissioner’s for a decision on the selection for the Movie
 Night film.

 The Park & Activities Commission held a brief discussion on this item.

REGULAR PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
MINUTES
APRIL 17, 2017  1
   CHAIR POPE moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  APPROVE “SING” AS THE FILM SELECTION FOR MOVIE NIGHT.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR POPE SO ORDERED.

  Chair Pope welcomed Commissioner Wroan to the Park & Activities Commission.

 COMMISSION ITEMS (VERBAL REPORTS)

 A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORT

 CHAIR POPE stated that she has several photos to forward to Director Clark regarding perimeter
 fencing issues.

 Director Clark stated that he heard from the fencing company today and they have not had time
 in their schedule to come back out to repair the fencing.

 COMMISSIONER RETZ inquired on the bid for painting the arena fence at Dapplegray. Director
 Clark stated that this project is ready to move forward.

 COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if that is something that the Boy Scouts could do. Director
 Clark stated that if it were part of a larger project, yes, but not as a single task.

 COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that the issues with the fence at Rockbluff Park have been
 ongoing for about a year and if the fencing company is not responding, then the City should look
 into alternatives. Director Clark stated that the second company on the list is Bennett
 Landscaping and they are local.

 COMMISSIONER GIGLIA at Ernie Howlett Park from Ring 3 to Ring 2, the hillside is extremely
 overgrown. Director Clark stated that he will send Bennett Landscape to take care of this.

 B.  RACE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE

 CHAIR POPE provided an update on the Race Subcommittee Meeting, which included the pre-
 registration fee, reviewing safety on the course, and volunteers. Director Clark stated that the
 race representative has volunteers available.

 COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI provided an update of the Race Subcommittee Meeting, which
 included the course, facility use, and sponsors.

 CHAIR POPE stated that the increase in fees will help in maintaining a reasonable net in proceeds
 to the Pepper Tree Foundation. There will also be more outreach to the Middle and High Schools.
 Director Clark stated that the coach of Peninsula High School should be bringing in 50 additional
 runners.

 COMMISSIONER WROAN inquired about group rates. Director Clark stated that there is a group
 rate and the High School will be able to take advantage of that discounted rate.

 C.  CITY CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE

 COMMISSIONER GIGLIA provided an update on the City Celebration Subcomittee meeting,
 which included discussion on the layout for the event, review of the budget with focus on
 equipment rental, and determining shared costs with Betty’s Foundation. The association with
 Betty’s Foundation is going well and they should be bringing in significantly more attendees to the
 event. Cliff with Betty’s Foundation has done a great job with advertising artwork including the
 banners. At the next meeting, Director Clark will be bringing in someone who is knowledgeable
 on all Health Department requirements. There was also discussion on the bus company for the
 event.

 CHAIR POPE stated that the planning of the event is going very well and stated that the Betty’s
 Foundation is bringing good things to the event, including their experience with professional
 musical events.

 There being no objection, CHAIR POPE ordered to receive and file these items.

REGULAR PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
MINUTES
APRIL 17, 2017  2
  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (VERBAL REPORTS)

 A.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE – MAY 6

 Director Clark stated that if the Commissioners would like to participate, please let him know.

 B.  HOWLETT PARK PLAY EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT PROJECT UPDATE

 Director Clark stated that the playground equipment has been installed. A concrete contractor
 will be coming out this week to put the forms and the perimeter barrier around the site.

 C.  LOS ANGELES COUNTY MEASURE “A” GRANT FUNDING INFORMATION

 Director Clark stated that he will be attending a meeting at Janice Hahn’s office on May 10 th,
 where she will be discussing what type of funding the 4th District will be getting. From Prop A, the
 City will continue to get funding for parks or recreation facilities.

 D.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK MURAL RIBBON CUTTING CEREMONY – MAY 15TH

 Director Clark stated that the Mural Ribbon Cutting Ceremony will be held on May 15th at 6:00
 p.m.

 E.  PV STREET FAIR & MUSIC FESTIVAL BOOTH SIGN-UP SHEET, JUNE 10-11TH

 Director Clark stated that he is sending around the sign-up sheet for the Peppertree Foundation
 Booth at the PV Street Fair event.

 MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MARCH 28, 2017

 There being no objection, CHAIR POPE ordered to receive and file these items.

 FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

 COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA inquired about PVDN and Narbonne. Director Clark stated that
 the City Council has a contract with the Rolling Hills Country Club and until their structure is
 completed, they will continue to use that site.

 Director Clark stated that at the Policy Development meeting there was discussion on the Land
 Conservancy funding the construction of a new structure at the Nature Center to replace the old
 Community Center. The second floor may be used as offices for the Land Conservancy staff.

 ADJOURNMENT

 COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  ADJOURN THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES MEETING

 THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR ROMANELLI adjourned the meeting at 7:40 p.m. to the
 Adjourned Parks & Activities Commission Meeting of MAY 15, 2017 at 6:30 p.m. at Ernie Howlett
 Park, 25851 Hawthorne Blvd., Rolling Hills Estates.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _________________________
  Carol Corea  Douglas R. Prichard
  Minutes Secretary  City Clerk

REGULAR PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
MINUTES
APRIL 17, 2017  3
